Sam (CS): Heads up — Brightloop onboarding stuck, their SDK calls failing with auth. Error shows 'invalid_kid' in our logs. They're worried about renewal if we don't unblock by EOD.
Alejandro: Can you paste the raw Authorization header and a sample token? Is this coming from Node/browser/mobile?
Sam (CS): Node 16 server. Header looks like `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. I DM'd a redacted token. Client also sent this snippet of the JWT header they decoded:
```json
{
  \"alg\": \"RS256\",
  \"typ\": \"JWT\",
  \"kid\": \"aGVsbG8rMTIz\"
}
```
Alejandro: Hmm kid has `+` when decoded? That looks like standard base64 (with +/) instead of base64url. Could be they exported from their HSM as standard base64. @Maria (AE) — any key rotations today that could explain remapped kid names?
Maria (AE): No rotations for Brightloop. We did an unrelated rotation earlier for another customer. Client mentioned they imported our sample key into their HSM and re-exported it; they might have changed encoding.
Alejandro: On our side we map kid -> active_kms_key using a strict regexp that expects base64url (no + or /). If the kid contains `+` or `=`, our lookup fails. I can relax the matcher to normalize both base64 and base64url, but need a repro.
Sam (CS): Repro steps from Brightloop: POST /v1/init with `Authorization` header, they get 401 JSON:
```json
{ \"error\": \"invalid_kid\", \"detail\": \"unknown signing key\" }
```
They say verifying the token locally with our published public JWK works fine.
Alejandro: Ask them to run this small check and paste the `kid` only:
```bash
node -e \"console.log(Buffer.from(process.argv[1],'base64').toString())\" aGVsbG8rMTIz
```
That will show if their export is standard base64 vs base64url.
Sam (CS): Sent that. Client replied: their HSM exported `aGVsbG8rMTIz` which decodes to a value containing `+` and was exported as standard base64 with `+/`.
Alejandro: That explains it. We expect base64url (no `+`/`/`). Quick mitigation: I'll add a normalization step that accepts both encodings for kid lookups and log normalized hits. Plan: change + tests (30m), canary to staging (1h), prod deploy in ~2-3h.
Maria (AE): I'll flag this account as renewal_at_risk in CRM until onboarding completes and schedule a call at 10:30 PST to keep the customer in the loop.
Sam (CS): Client is okay with either us patching or re-exporting URL-safe keys. They said if we can't push prod in 2h they'll re-export. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for commit abc123 — runtime-auth-normalize (Alejandro). Staging URL: https://staging.redwood/ci/abc123
Alejandro: Canary looks good; deployed to prod and monitoring logs for `invalid_kid` spikes. Added telemetry metric `auth.normalized_kid.count`.
Sam (CS): Brightloop confirmed tokens accepted and initial requests succeeded. On-call appreciated the fast turnaround. Marking onboarding unblocked.
Maria (AE): Follow-up action — add a note to the onboarding checklist: 'verify KMS export encoding (base64url vs base64) and sample kid decode step'. I'll update enablement docs and the quickstart.
Sam (CS): Leaving this thread closed unless anything else pops up. Thanks team!
